title: Reading Nutrition Labels: What to Actually Look For

authorship.recommended_normalized_author: Healthy Weight Literacy Foundation Editorial Team

primary_question: What should I actually look for when reading a nutrition label?
reader_intent: Get a concise, practical walkthrough of the most important parts of a nutrition label.
desired_reader_outcome: Reader knows to check serving size first, compare added sugars/sodium/saturated fat, look for fiber/vitamin D/calcium/iron/potassium, and question front-of-package marketing claims.

claims.proposition: AHA recommends limiting added sugars to 25g (women) / 36g (men) per day; sodium limit 2,300mg/day.

internal_link_recommendations.reason: More comprehensive near-duplicate; should be consulted together until merged.

disposition_reason: This reader job (how to read a nutrition label) is substantially duplicated by reading-nutrition-labels-weight-health, which additionally covers vitamins/minerals and per-meal protein guidance. This article's distinct value — the FDA 2020 label-format-update context and the front-of-package marketing-claims caution — is worth preserving in the merge.
recommended_rewrite_scope: Fold the FDA 2020 label-update context and marketing-claims section into the survivor.
